The build-up to the match at the Stade Velodrome was marred by incidents in the stands, including the throwing of projectiles and flares between the two sets of supporters. Ligue 1 club Marseille said it was ""working to understand the precise circumstances of these incidents"". Levski Sofia coach Julio Velazquez stated the clashes were ""unacceptable for football"" while his Marseille counterpart Bruno Genesio labelled them ""very regrettable"". With 10 minutes to go until kick-off, several Marseille fans ran from a home stand, appearing to pursue a group of Bulgarian supporters. They breached the stand designated for away fans, which housed around 500 supporters of the Bulgarian domestic champions. ""Five people were taken to hospital with eye injuries, head trauma and a dislocated shoulder,"" the Marseille police prefecture told AFP. ""Six others were treated on site for various wounds."" The police source said all the people injured were Bulgarian and there was ""no information at this stage regarding any arrests"". Security personnel managed to restore calm, allowing the game to kick-off on time, although there were a few further flare-ups between the fans, notably during the half-time break. ""It's a very regrettable episode. These are incidents which are unacceptable for football,"" said Velazquez. ""I support the fans who were caught up in this incident. I hope nothing serious has happened. I'm very saddened by this situation."" The home side won the match 1-0 thanks to an Amine Gouiri penalty in the 28th minute. ""We are living through violent times in our society, so this is very, very regrettable,"" added Genesio. Bulgarian President Iliana Iotova said she found footage from the game ""shocking"" in a statement posted on social media. ""The attacks against the Bulgarian fans desecrate one of the great games that brings millions of people together around the world,"" she added. ""Everyone should be able to support their team without being afraid for their safety."" Offside, Levski Sofia. Kristian Dimitrov is caught offside. column1: V,FINALS: WALLABIES TEAM TO PLAY IRELAND IN 3 v 3 FINAL - Super Rugby,2026-11-26 21:18:16,"West Harbour junior Allan Alaalatoa will become the 14th Wallabies centurion when he runs out onto Allianz Stadium Twickenham against Ireland in London on Friday night local time. Wallaby number 896, Alaalatoa will also co-captain the side for their final Test of 2026 which sees the two third ranked sides from the Southern and Northern Hemispheres square off as part of the Nations Championship Finals Weekend. Having made his Test debut in 2016 against New Zealand, Alaalatoa became the 85th captain of his country in 2022 and has led the side a further seven times ahead of this weekend. On the other end of the spectrum, James Ramm has been selected to make his Test debut on the left wing. Born and raised in Sydney, the 28-year-old has been patient in waiting to fulfil his dream, spending time with the NSW Waratahs followed by a successful stint with the Northampton Saints in the UK Premiership before signing to return to Australian Rugby with the Western Force. He’s one of two potential debutants with Teddy Wilson named as the scrumhalf replacement on the bench – the former Junior Wallabies captain in line to become the 16th son of a Wallaby to pull on the gold jersey, following in the footsteps of his father David who featured in two Rugby World Cups, including the 1999 side that lifted the Webb Ellis Cup in Cardiff. Elsewhere, Wallaby number 836 Kurtley Beale has earned a remarkable recall to the gold jersey – named on the bench, four years since his last Test appearance. Alaalatoa will be joined by Isaac Kailea and Brandon Paenga-Amosa in the run on front row, with Josh Canham and Jeremy Williams the starting lock pairing. Williams showing his robustness, earning selection in every Test for the Wallabies over the last two years. Tom Hooper is named at blindside flanker in a new-look back row that features Carlo Tizzano at openside and Rob Valetini in the number eight jersey. Springfield Hawks junior Kalani Thomas has earned his first Test start after his strong impact off the pine against Wales in Cardiff, forming a familiar partnership with club teammate Carter Gordon who is again selected at flyhalf. The midfield remains unchanged from the side that defeated Wales with Len Ikitau and Joseph-Aukuso Suaalii continuing to build their combination, while Max Jorgensen and Tom Wright round out the back three alongside Ramm. Jorgensen and Wright both named in all 14 Wallabies Tests this year. The Wallabies have selected a six forwards, two backs bench split, with Josh Nasser, Angus Bell and Taniela Tupou the replacement front row, with Fraser McReight and co-captain Harry Wilson the remaining forward cover. Bell and McReight the other players to feature in every match of 2026. Wallabies Head Coach Les Kiss said: “Reaching 100 Test matches for your country is a remarkable achievement and it’s only fitting that Allan leads the side out as co-captain for such a monumental occasion. “He is a talismanic figure within the group, and I know the whole squad and support staff will be doing everything they can to make this rare milestone a memorable one for him, his family and for us. “We’ve taken some steps forward, grown our game and tested our squad depth this year as a squad and I know the team is highly motivated to put in a performance that reflects the hard work put in by everyone in our final Test.” Wallabies team to play Ireland at Allianz Stadium Twickenham in London 1    Isaac Kailea (12 Tests) - #975; Harlequin Junior Rugby Club

V,Ford v Ferrari 2. GT41 Hypercar debuts at Lions Thanksgiving game - The Detroit News,2026-11-26 18:00:00,"Forget Lions v. Bears. Get ready for Ford v. Ferrari, Part 2. Sixty years after the Ford GT40 defeated Ferrari at the world’s most prestigious endurance race, the 24 Hours of Le Mans, the Dearborn automaker is going back to reclaim its title with the GT41 Hypercar introduced at Ford Field ahead of the Detroit Lions-Chicago Bears game on Thanksgiving. A new, pulse-pounding “Go Like Hell” 60-second film introducing the Hypercar, voiced by movie star Matt Damon, will then air at halftime of the national CBS broadcast. The TV spot connects Ford’s legendary 1966 Le Mans win with Ford Racing’s return to the World Endurance Championship’s top class. The V8-powered GT41 is an homage to the thundering GT40 — its alphanumeric badge reflecting that the low, sleek prototype is a mere 41 inches tall (the GT40 was 40 inches high). Just like in the 1960s, Ferrari has been the car to beat at Le Mans this decade, winning three of the last four races. To add spice to the narrative, Ford will also be competing for Le Mans trophy against crosstown rival Cadillac and its V-Series.R Hypercar, which qualified on the Le Mans front row the last two years. “Since the '60s, we've always wondered, when is the right time for us to go back for the overall win at Le Mans?” said Will Ford, Ford Racing general manager and son of Ford Executive Chairman Bill Ford, in an exclusive interview. “It’s the right time to go back. We're doing a lot of development work in house that we haven't done before ... to better integrate our motorsport development and production vehicle development. Winning Le Mans next year for the overall win — that's the goal.” Ford’s racing history stretches back 125 years ago when Bill Ford’s great-grandfather won the Grosse Pointe Sweepstakes race to attract investors to his fledgling company. But the GT40’s triumph in 1966 (and subsequent dominance of the race from 1966-69) established Ford at the pinnacle of global motorsport, a position it still holds today with its Red Bull partnership in Formula One, Mustang GT3 racing program, and now the GT41. “Our 1-2-3 triumph at Le Mans in 1966 remains one of the defining moments in motorsport history,” said Bill Ford. “We cherish that history, but we are driven by the opportunity to take on new and greater challenges. The Ford GT41 is exactly the kind of audacious, go-like-hell project that gets our blood pumping. It’s our chance to return to Le Mans and compete for the outright win.” The 1966 feat inspired the Oscar-winning 2019 Hollywood blockbuster ""Ford v Ferrari."" But a lot has changed in six decades. The GT40 ran in a pre-aerodynamic era when ground effects was a novel art. The GT40 was built for brute force — its 7-liter V-8 hitting 201 mph on the long, three-mile Mulsanne straight to outpace 193-mph Ferrari 330 P3s. Today’s Hypercars are designed like upside-down airplanes, their sophisticated front and rear wings sucking the car to the ground for high cornering speeds. The famed Mulsanne straight has been sectioned by two chicanes, putting more emphasis on race cars’ cornering abilities in addition to outright speed. Balancing straight-line speed and cornering ability is the key to winning. The Cadillac V-Series.R was the fastest car on Mulsanne in 2026 at 218 mph. The GT41 Hypercar will make its WEC debut at the 2027 Qatar race March 27, part of a nine-race international schedule with the 24 Hours of Le Mans June 12-13 as its centerpiece. The series makes its U.S. stop in Austin, Texas, at Circuit of the America on Sept. 12. Ford also enters a Mustang GT3 race car in the production-based LMGT3 class. The GT41 is powered by a ribcage-rattling, 5.4-liter, naturally aspirated V-8 engine based on the same Coyote architecture that motivates the Mustang production car. Per international Hypercar regulations, it is paired with a hybrid system common to other cars in class, including racers from Cadillac, Ferrari and 2026 Le Mans champion Toyota. ""Revealing the Ford GT41 is a significant moment for everyone involved in this program,” said Dan Sayers, Ford Racing Hypercar program manager. “It's the result of an enormous amount of work across our engineering, design and development teams and an important milestone on our journey towards 2027. We know the scale of the challenge ahead — the level of competition in Hypercar is incredibly high.” Alongside the car's development, Ford Racing has assembled an experienced international driver lineup comprising Logan Sargeant, Tom Blomqvist, Matt Campbell, Sebastian Priaulx, Mike Rockenfeller and Nick Yelloly. The team will also benefit from the expertise of Tom Dillmann, confirmed earlier this month as Ford Racing's reserve driver for 2027. ""The GT41 testing program has been really positive so far,” said Sargeant. “There's been a huge amount of work going on behind the scenes and it's encouraging to see that progress translating onto the track. The official reveal of our Ford GT41 is a really special moment for everyone involved and makes 2027 feel that much closer.” The GT41 has been testing in full camouflage on international tracks, and Thursday’s debut revealed the Hypercar’s full design dressed in a blue-on-blue wrap. The design incorporates hidden symbols of Americana, including the American flag, bald eagle and Spirit of Detroit. The final racing livery will be revealed closer to the Qatar race in 2027. “I will just say that it (will be) iconically Ford Racing Blue,” said Will Ford. “We're the blue car going around the track, and we're going to stick to that for a very long time.” In addition to competing for motorsports glory, Ford Racing’s Hypercar development is part of a racing portfolio that spans off-road and on-road racing. The Hypercar hybrid system is a showcase for Ford’s signature V-8 — but also informs development of production car electrification systems along with the Red Bull F1 program. The exchange is a two-way street with expertise from Ford Motor Co.'s global engineering operations assisting the development of racing programs. “This is about more than one race,” said Ford Racing Global Director Mark Rushbrook. “It's about building a competitive motorsport program that delivers value across our business and helps shape the future of Ford Racing."" Henry Payne is auto critic for The Detroit News.
